title: Artificial Analysis: AI model and API provider benchmark landing page
answer: This is the landing page for Artificial Analysis, a site that compares AI models and API hosting providers using independent benchmarks for quality, price, output speed and latency. Its most useful contribution in the supplied text is a set of clear metric definitions, including pass^5 reliability for AA-AnalystAgent, Intelligence Index evaluation cost, tokens per second, and provider endpoint accuracy preservation. The text does not mention healthcare, medical tasks or clinical reasoning, so it does not itself support a claim that Artificial Analysis ranks models on medical tasks.

sections.body: Artificial Analysis publishes this page as a comparison and analysis of AI models and API hosting providers. The supplied text describes independent benchmarks across key performance metrics including quality, price, output speed and latency. It lists model providers and API hosting providers, and it defines several metrics used on the site. No publication date is stated. The harvested text is a landing page, not a full report, and it does not mention healthcare or medical tasks.
sections.heading: What this source is

sections.body: The page presents itself as a comparison and analysis of AI models and API hosting providers, with independent benchmarks across quality, price, output speed and latency. It explains that model weights availability is indicated, with models labelled Commercial Use Restricted if commercial use is limited by conditions, and Non-commercial if the license prohibits commercial use. It defines AA-AnalystAgent as a benchmark for end-to-end quantitative analysis on real-world spreadsheets and documents, where pass^5 is the share of questions answered correctly on all five attempts, measuring reliability rather than how often a model reaches a correct answer. It defines the cost to run evaluations in the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, calculated using input, cache hit, cache write, reasoning and answer token prices and the number of tokens used across evaluations, excluding repeats. It defines tokens per second as tokens received while the model is generating tokens, after the first chunk for streaming models. It says figures represent the model's first-party API or the median across providers where no first-party API is available. It defines a composite measure of how much of a model's accuracy a provider endpoint preserves, from re-running BFCL v4-500, HLE-250 and AA-LCR-25 against that endpoint, expressed as a percentage of a self-hosted reference where one exists, with lower scores indicating accuracy lost to quantisation, sampling defaults or other endpoint-side configuration. It states scores are point-in-time snapshots and links to methodology.
sections.heading: What it says

sections.body: The supplied text gives no numerical benchmark results and no healthcare figures. It defines pass^5 as the share of AA-AnalystAgent questions answered correctly on all five attempts. It says the Intelligence Index evaluation cost uses input, cache hit, cache write, reasoning and answer token prices and token counts, excluding repeats. It defines tokens per second as tokens received while generating, after the first chunk for streaming models. It defines provider endpoint accuracy preservation from re-running BFCL v4-500, HLE-250 and AA-LCR-25, expressed as a percentage of a self-hosted reference where one exists. It labels models Commercial Use Restricted or Non-commercial based on licence conditions. It lists model providers and API hosting providers but gives no scores for them.
sections.heading: Figures and claims worth noting

sections.body: A reader following AI in healthcare would use this source as a vendor-neutral reference for how Artificial Analysis compares models and API providers on general performance, price, speed and latency. It is useful for understanding the metrics behind such comparisons, including reliability, evaluation cost and endpoint accuracy preservation. However, the supplied text does not mention healthcare, medical tasks or clinical reasoning, so it does not support the claim that Artificial Analysis ranks models on medical tasks. The source can help a healthcare-focused reader ask better questions about provider performance, but it offers no healthcare-specific evidence in this text.
sections.heading: What it means for AI in Healthcare

sections.body: This is a landing page with little substantive content beyond metric definitions and provider lists. It states no publication date. It gives no benchmark results, no methodology detail beyond a link, and no healthcare or medical coverage. It appears to be a commercial site for model and API provider analysis, though the text does not state funding or commercial relationships. The harvested text is partial and does not show the underlying evaluations or any medical task results.
